clues.title: Google car: white pickup, front antenna
text: Costa Rica’s Generation 4 imagery was captured using a large **white pickup truck**. In many locations, it is either fully or partially visible, but can occasionally be entirely blurred out. There is an antenna attached to the front of the car.

NOTE: The Panamanian truck is almost always [fully blurred out](https://maps.app.goo.gl/SXjYfDTrfFwZTWLs8). The truck used in [Ecuador](https://maps.app.goo.gl/dSweUPGTkgTasq9B7) does not have an antenna.
clues.summary: A large white pickup truck with an antenna on the front, often partly visible but sometimes fully blurred. Panama's truck is almost always fully blurred, and Ecuador's has no antenna.

differs.how: Truck is almost always fully blurred

clues.title: Plate: short, white, blue text
text: Costa Rican licence plates are typically short and white with **blue text**, giving them a light blue tint through the blur.
clues.summary: Plates are short and white with blue text, which gives a light blue tint through the blur. This helps tell it apart from Panama.

differs.how: Panamanian plates are not tinted light blue

clues.title: Landscape: lush hills, volcanoes, rainforest
text: Costa Rica is a mostly** lush tropical country**, with rolling hills, agricultural lowlands, peaky volcanoes running through the centre of the country, as well as dense rainforests dotted around.

images.caption: Four dirt tracks through green farmland and forest

clues.summary: A lush tropical country with rolling hills, farmland lowlands, pointed volcanoes through the middle and patches of dense rainforest.

clues.title: Houses: pastel concrete, fences, barred windows
text: Costa Rican architecture is less colonial than that of Panama. Few houses have proper tiled roofs, with dark red sheet metal or dark red plastic tiles being more common. Buildings typically have **pastel-coloured concrete walls** and are usually either a low **single-family** house or **boxy two-storey** structure. They are often heavily guarded with **fences **and **barred windows**, to the point that it can be hard to even see a building on many streets.
clues.summary: Pastel-coloured concrete houses, low single-family homes or boxy two-storey ones, with dark red metal or plastic roofs. Heavy fences and barred windows can hide the buildings. Less colonial than Panama.

differs.how: More colonial style, with tiled roofs

clues.title: Language: Spanish
text: Like in most of Latin America, **Spanish** is the official language of Costa Rica.
NOTE: In Brazil, they speak Portuguese.
clues.summary: Spanish is the language, as in most of Latin America. Brazil speaks Portuguese.

clues.title: Sign: stop sign says ALTO
text: Like in Mexico, Panama and Guatemala, Costa Rican stop signs display the word **“ALTO”**.
NOTE: Stop signs in [Panama](https://goo.gl/maps/LaAjCE36HSZziiCg8) use a thicker font. Furthermore, in the rest of Spanish Latin America they say “PARE”.
clues.summary: Stop signs say ALTO, as in Mexico, Panama and Guatemala. The rest of Spanish-speaking Latin America writes PARE. Panama's ALTO has a thicker font.

clues.title: Taxis: red
text: Red taxis are the standard in Costa Rica.
NOTE: Panama uses yellow taxis.
clues.summary: Red taxis are the standard. Panama uses yellow taxis.

clues.title: Pole: long silver insulators
text: Costa Rica uses **long silver insulators**.

NOTE: Panama uses a variety of insulators, some of which are also [long silver insulators](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fVdRraxxpbLSgzWdA), they also use [short silver](https://maps.app.goo.gl/15arUFZ8Zi7XbEii7), [long black](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Ch37q5EZoLi7Xe9z9), [UFO](https://maps.app.goo.gl/GbzUD5YTpd9RXAb27) and [white mushroom](https://maps.app.goo.gl/2fAxTEEveNTe6Pdd9) insulators. Additionally, Brazil can have long silver insulators. Lastly, Ecuador uses UFO and mushroom insulators.

images.caption: Red circles mark the three long silver insulators on the pole

clues.summary: Poles carry long silver insulators. Panama has these among other kinds, and Brazil can have them too, while Ecuador uses UFO and mushroom ones.

clues.title: Pole: low even crossbar, 2+1 insulators
text: One of the most common pole tops is an even crossbar with uneven insulators, meaning there is one on one side and two on the other. Additionally, the crossbar is further down on the pole than usual.

NOTE: 2 on 1 insulator poles with a low crossbar can also be found in Panama. However, poles in Costa Rica usually feature support bars, while this is much more rare on [Panamanian poles.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/nUBSxGGYTvWqCygu8)

images.caption: Red arrow and numbers mark a low even crossbar with 2 insulators on one side and 1 on the other

clues.summary: A common pole top has an even crossbar sitting low on the pole, with one insulator on one side and two on the other. Costa Rican poles usually have support bars. Panama's rarely do.

differs.how: Panamanian poles rarely have support bars

clues.title: Pole: single insulator on the side at the top
text: Poles that have a single insulator attached to the side at the top of the pole are commonly found in Costa Rica.

images.caption: A red circle marks the single insulator on the side at the top of the pole

clues.summary: Poles with a single insulator fixed to the side near the top are common.

clues.title: Pole: lamp with a blue dot on top
text: Utility poles in Costa Rica feature a lamp with a blue dot on the top, similarly to other Latin American countries like Panama, Colombia and Brazil.

images.caption: Red circles mark the blue dot on top of each streetlamp

clues.summary: Utility poles carry a lamp with a blue dot on the top, as in Panama, Colombia and Brazil.

clues.title: Pole: thin metal crossbar bent into an L
text: Also common is this thin metal crossbar that is bent 90 degrees to form an L-shape.
NOTE: Also commonly found in Panama, Colombia and Ecuador. However, poles with crossbars are generally not as common in Panama as they are in Costa Rica.

images.caption: Red marks show a thin metal crossbar bent into an L, with insulators at both ends

clues.summary: A thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees into an L shape is common. Panama, Colombia and Ecuador have it too, but crossbars are less common in Panama.

clues.title: Sign back: cross brace behind warning signs
text: Many road signs have a distinct **cross **on the back. This is most common on diamond-shaped warning signs, while others are mostly attached regularly.
NOTE: Signs in Colombia almost always have a cross at the back, but they use white signposts.
clues.summary: Many road signs have a distinct cross on the back, most often on diamond warning signs. Colombia almost always has the cross, but on white posts.

differs.how: Cross on almost every sign, with white signposts

clues.title: Bollard: orange board with 3 black circles
text: The equivalent of a bollard in Costa Rica would be these vertical **orange boards** with **3 black circles** on them.
clues.summary: Instead of bollards, look for vertical orange boards with three black circles.

clues.title: Electricity meter: round, big metal box beside
text: Electricity counters in Costa Rica are circular and often have a big metal box alongside them.
NOTE: Circular counters may be found in other North American countries, most notably Mexico.
clues.summary: Round electricity meters, often with a large metal box next to them. Mexico and other North American countries have round meters too.

clues.title: Ads: beer with black eagle mascot
text: Imperial beer ads with its** black eagle mascot** are a common sight in Costa Rica.
clues.summary: Ads for a beer with a black eagle mascot are common.

clues.title: Provinces: names sometimes on signs
text: The provinces are sometimes written on signs, so they are useful to know. We will also refer to them in the clues below.
clues.summary: Province names are sometimes written on signs, so it helps to know them.

clues.title: Flags: each province has its own flag
text: Each province has their own provincial flag.
clues.summary: Every province has its own flag, which you may see on buildings.

clues.title: Phone numbers: area codes moderately useful
text: Area codes are moderately useful to learn for Costa Rica.
clues.summary: Area codes help a bit with locating a round. Worth learning if you want extra detail.

clues.title: Pole: large black or white stickers with numbers
text: Poles are sometimes marked with large [black](https://maps.app.goo.gl/VcCnYBtpTctWDzPj8) or [white](https://maps.app.goo.gl/BLrafkVmtcoLRzqMA) stickers, containing multiple lines of text. The **first digit **of the topmost number is province-specific.

_For more specific information, please see this research _[document](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1v0JPX6oGBOsDQ8x68jGbO3LpWcwU9UcNn9GV3bcwW1M/edit?slide=id.g3790a800eb2_0_129#slide=id.g3790a800eb2_0_129)_ created by L’Heureux Traité._
clues.summary: Poles sometimes carry big black or white stickers with several lines of text. The first digit of the top number tells you the province.

clues.title: Pole: one insulator one side, two on the other
text: Asymmetrical pole tops with one insulator on one side of the pole and two on the other are found in and around San José.
NOTE: Fully asymmetrical pole tops with all insulators on one side of the pole can be found all across the country.
clues.summary: Poles with one insulator on one side and two on the other are found around the capital. Poles with all insulators on one side are found across the country.

clues.title: Pole: numbers made of wire
text: Pole attachments consisting of numbers made out of wires are found in central Alajuela and over the border in Heredia province.

images.caption: Numbers made of wire on a dark pole, left of the pole in the foreground

clues.summary: Pole attachments shaped like numbers made of wire are found in central Alajuela and over the border in Heredia.

clues.title: Pole: white plate with black letters
text: **White pole plates** with black lettering are specific to the Greater Metropolitan Area. They are usually attached to the pole using metal bands, although these may sometimes be [missing](https://maps.app.goo.gl/QbxrouQ556tLVWo29).
clues.summary: White pole plates with black lettering are specific to the Greater Metropolitan Area. They are usually held on by metal bands, though sometimes missing.

clues.title: Pole: blue P-XXXXX code
text: Usually blue lettering forming a P-XXXXX code with or without the accompanying white background can be found in western Cartago province.
clues.summary: Blue lettering forming a P-XXXXX code, with or without a white background, is found in western Cartago province.

clues.title: Pole: small black stickers with a QR code
text: Small black stickers with a **QR code** on the bottom can be seen around Corralillo, south of San José.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on a small black QR sticker on the pole

clues.summary: Small black stickers with a QR code at the bottom appear around Corralillo, south of San José.

clues.title: Pole: tall yellow paint, 3 numbered sections
text: Yellow pole paint that is** tall** and has **3 sections** with numbers is mainly found in Puntarenas and southern Alajuela provinces.
clues.summary: Tall yellow pole paint divided into three sections with numbers, mainly in Puntarenas and southern Alajuela.

clues.title: Pole: short yellow paint
text: Yellow pole paint that is **shorter **and contains all the numbers **without dividing lines** is mainly found in Guanacaste and northwestern Alajuela provinces.
clues.summary: Shorter yellow pole paint with all the numbers and no dividing lines, mainly in Guanacaste and northwestern Alajuela.

clues.title: Pole: yellow paint, 2 sections
text: Yellow pole paint divided into** 2 sections** with** horizontal characters** at the **bottom **are almost unique to southern Alajuela province.
NOTE: You can find 2 sectioned yellow pole paint without the horizontal characters at the bottom almost everywhere in Costa Rica.
clues.summary: Yellow pole paint in two sections with horizontal characters at the bottom is almost only found in southern Alajuela. Two sections without the horizontal characters are found almost everywhere.

clues.title: Pole: black sticker, yellow letters, low
text: These black pole stickers with **yellow lettering**, located near the bottom of the pole, are limited to western Guanacaste province and the Nicoya peninsula.
clues.summary: Black pole stickers with yellow lettering, low on the pole, are only in western Guanacaste and the Nicoya peninsula.

clues.title: Landscape: flat lowlands, grey dirt
text: North of the mountains lie the largely flat Caribbean **Lowlands**, characterised by extensive agriculture, grey dirt and a good number of straight roads. Although overcast coverage is common in this area, some locations can be rather [sunny](https://maps.app.goo.gl/N4eAcvDuwTzWmg4n7).
clues.summary: North of the mountains the Caribbean lowlands are largely flat, with lots of farming, grey dirt and straight roads. Overcast is common but some places are sunny.

clues.title: Coverage: dry-season shots in the west
text: A lot of the coverage in western Costa Rica was captured during the **dry season**.
clues.summary: A lot of the western coverage was taken in the dry season, so it looks drier and browner.

clues.title: Plants: banana plantations in the east
text: Most of the **banana **plantations are found in Limón province.
NOTE: Wild banana plants and planted bananas in gardens are found throughout most of the country.
clues.summary: Most banana plantations are in Limón province in the east. Wild bananas and garden bananas are found almost everywhere.

clues.title: Plants: oil palm plantations on the coast
text: The majority of **oil palm** plantations are found along the coast in Puntarenas province. A few smaller plantations are located in Limón province.
NOTE: A few oil palms can be found here and there throughout the country, especially on the east coast but they’re not part of any plantations.
clues.summary: Most oil palm plantations are along the coast of Puntarenas province, with a few smaller ones in Limón. Single oil palms appear all over, especially on the east coast.

clues.title: Plants: pineapple plantations
text: **Pineapple **plantations can be seen in western Limón province, northern Alajuela province as well as around the town of Buenos Aires in Puntarenas province.
clues.summary: Pineapple plantations are in western Limón, northern Alajuela, and around Buenos Aires in Puntarenas.

clues.title: Plants: sugarcane, silvery tufts in the south
text: **Sugarcane **plantations can be found in multiple areas across the country, but the major areas are usually distinguishable based on landscape. In the southern area around San Isidro de El General and Buenos Aires you can find sugarcane plantations in [bloom](https://maps.app.goo.gl/j6rWvHbxbdmVnqwRA) with silvery tufts of strands at the top of the plants.
clues.summary: Sugarcane is grown in several areas. In the south, around San Isidro de El General and Buenos Aires, it often flowers with silvery tufts on top.

clues.title: Fields: rice paddies with raised edges
text: **Rice **fields are mostly found south of the town of Bagaces in Guanacaste province. Some fields are harvested or just recently planted but can be recognized by the [raised edges](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6mzgeZSYFtH7G2Nt8) around the paddies.
clues.summary: Rice fields are mostly south of Bagaces in Guanacaste. Even harvested or newly planted ones show raised edges around the paddies.

clues.title: Plants: coffee plantations in the central valley
text: The majority of **coffee **plantations are located throughout the central valley.
clues.summary: Most coffee plantations are throughout the central valley.

clues.title: Plants: cassava plantations in the east
text: **Cassava **plantations are most commonly found in western Limón province.
clues.summary: Cassava plantations are most common in western Limón province.

clues.title: Trees: teak with tall trunks
text: **Teak **is recognisable for their tall straight trunks and round glossy, yellow-green leaves and is most common in Guanacaste.

images.caption: Teak trees with tall bare trunks; the inset circle, top left, shows their large leaves

clues.summary: Teak has tall straight trunks and round, glossy, yellow-green leaves, and is most common in Guanacaste.

clues.title: Trees: thick trunk, big umbrella crown
text: **Guanacaste trees **can be recognised by their thick trunk and characteristically large, umbrella-shaped crown. They are mostly seen in the eponymous Guanacaste province.
clues.summary: Guanacaste trees have thick trunks and a large umbrella-shaped crown. They are mostly seen in Guanacaste province.

clues.title: Palms: upward leaves that droop slightly
text: Mainly growing along the southern coast, **Attalea palms** can be recognised by the upwards facing leaves that droop slightly.
clues.summary: Attalea palms have upward-pointing leaves that droop a little. They grow mainly along the southern coast.

clues.title: Palms: round crown, messy bunches, spiky trunk
text: **Macaw palms** are common in western Costa Rica and can be recognised by the long and disheveled looking broods that form an almost round crown. They also usually have a spiky trunk as well.
clues.summary: Macaw palms are common in the west, with long, messy-looking leaf clusters forming a nearly round crown and usually a spiky trunk.

clues.title: Rocks: dark volcanic rocks
text: Dark **volcanic rocks** can be found in most of central Costa Rica, but are more common around Guapiles, Limón Province and around the Miravalles Volcano on the border of Alajuela and Guanacaste provinces.
clues.summary: Dark volcanic rocks are found in much of central Costa Rica, and more so around Guápiles in Limón and around the Miravalles Volcano.

clues.title: Taxis: red with yellow triangles
text: Taxis in Costa Rica are [red](https://maps.app.goo.gl/inEA3C7FKWcQ1Sqq5), featuring yellow triangles on the sides and top containing the city/town name as well as a letter code denoting the province.
clues.summary: Taxis are red with yellow triangles on the sides and roof showing the town name and a letter code for the province.

clues.title: City: valley, inclines, taller buildings
text: **San José** is the capital and by far the largest urban area in Costa Rica. Situated in a valley between multiple mountains, the roads have a noticeable incline. You will see many suburban neighbourhoods and [taller buildings](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cJGHc42e3oXrugMK8) than anywhere else in the country.
clues.summary: The capital sits in a valley between mountains, so roads climb and dip. You see lots of suburbs and the tallest buildings in the country.

clues.title: Fences: rough wooden branch or log fences
text: Simple fences made of irregular wooden branches or logs are found all over Costa Rica but much more prevalent in the west, compared to the planted tree rows or spiked concrete variants more common elsewhere.
clues.summary: Simple fences made of irregular branches or logs are found everywhere but much more in the west. Elsewhere, planted tree rows or spiked concrete fences are more common.

clues.title: Canals: large irrigation canals
text: Larger irrigation canals exist in the area south of Bagaces and Cañas in Guanacaste province.
clues.summary: Larger irrigation canals are found south of Bagaces and Cañas in Guanacaste province.

clues.title: Houses: on stilts, northeast coast
text: Houses on stilts are mostly found on the northeastern coast.
clues.summary: Houses raised on stilts are mostly found on the northeastern coast.

clues.title: Google car: antenna folded down
text: The antenna can occasionally be seen **folded down**, predominantly in the north and northeast of the country.

images.caption: Red circle at top left zooms in on the folded-down antenna on the roof of the white pickup

clues.summary: The antenna is occasionally folded down, mostly in the north and northeast.

clues.title: Street sign: green with a white emblem box
text: The entire municipality of San José consistently uses these **green **street signs with a **white rectangle** containing an emblem. Calle/Avenida streets are numerically ordered, increasing from downtown outwards.
clues.summary: The capital municipality consistently uses green street signs with a white rectangle holding an emblem. Calle and Avenida numbers increase from downtown outwards.

clues.title: Railways: only a few lines
text: There are only a few train tracks in Costa Rica. A few lines exist in the Greater Metropolitan Area, from which they go to Puntarenas in the west, and through Turrialba to Siquirres in the east, where it further continues southeast to Limón and to [Patio San Cristobal](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UwTxj8noX6TYdcKu7) to the northwest.
clues.summary: There are only a few train tracks: some in the Greater Metropolitan Area, one to the west coast, and one east through Turrialba to Siquirres, continuing to Limón and the northwest.

clues.title: Highways: only two concrete stretches
text: The only concrete highways are the eastern stretch of Ruta Nacional 18, and the divided Pan-American Highway ([RN 1](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mNZWwCKic8Ue2BXZ7)) from Liberia to the intersection with RN 18.
clues.summary: The only concrete highways are the eastern stretch of Ruta 18 and the divided Pan-American Highway (Ruta 1) from Liberia to Ruta 18.

clues.title: Highway: divided road through lush flat forest
text: Another major divided highway is the RN 32 from the intersection with RN 4 to Limón on the Caribbean coast. The road passes through lush forests in the generally flat Northern lowlands.
NOTE: Aside from the stretch of the RN 1 with concrete pavement, all other major divided highways are in close proximity to San José.
clues.summary: The RN 32 is a major divided highway from the junction with RN 4 to Limón on the Caribbean coast, through lush forests in the flat northern lowlands. Other divided highways are near the capital.

clues.title: Bollard: yellow, between the centre lines
text: From the “Route 32 Toll” close to the San José and Heredia border until where it intersects RN 4 west of Guapiles, the road uses yellow bollards placed between the centre road lines.
clues.summary: From the Route 32 toll near the San José and Heredia border to the junction with RN 4 west of Guápiles, yellow bollards sit between the centre lines.

clues.title: Follow car: yellow with two front windows
text: A** yellow follow car** with two front windows can be seen trailing the Google truck on RN 2 east of Palmar Norte and halfway up to Buenos Aires. The **river valley** also makes this section of road unique.

images.caption: A yellow follow car with two front windows, shown in the inset circle at left

clues.summary: A yellow follow car with two front windows trails the Google truck on RN 2 east of Palmar Norte, halfway to Buenos Aires. The river valley is also distinctive.

clues.title: Landmarks: wind turbine clusters
text: **Wind turbines** are found in a few clusters, mainly in Guanacaste province, but also [southwest of Cartago](https://maps.app.goo.gl/kinQ4DrYnX1DDAE78), over the province border in San José province. In Guanacaste, you’ll find them around [La Fortuna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UmgV5e75VdZt6U4BA), south and northwest of [Tilarán](https://maps.app.goo.gl/DsX2L86PBvAD4EYG6), around [Santa Cruz](https://maps.app.goo.gl/az1pUNDBrfYmXzYg6), and quite far north of Liberia around [road 917](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tKdvSioXF9jpiSbP6).
clues.summary: Wind turbines stand in a few clusters, mainly in Guanacaste (La Fortuna, Tilarán, Santa Cruz, north of Liberia) and southwest of Cartago.

clues.title: Road: bright white soil
text: Bright white soil roads likely place you just north of the city of Liberia, Guanacaste province.
clues.summary: Roads with bright white soil probably put you just north of Liberia in Guanacaste.

clues.title: Coverage: late evening and night shots
text: Late evening into night coverage can be found in the town of San Vito.
clues.summary: Late evening and night coverage is found in the southern town of San Vito.

clues.title: Vehicles: tuk-tuks on the coast
text: Tuk-Tuks can be seen around Puerto Viejo de Talamanca on the northeast coast, and less often around Nosara on the west coast.
clues.summary: Tuk-tuks are seen around Puerto Viejo de Talamanca on the northeast coast, and less often around Nosara on the west coast.

clues.title: Filming crew: black Toyota with camera crew
text: You can spot [Rainbolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Rainbolt) himself, or the **filming crew** atop a **black Toyota** around the town of La Fortuna, Alajuela Province.
clues.summary: A well-known streamer, or his film crew on top of a black Toyota, can be spotted around La Fortuna in Alajuela.

clues.title: Backpack: downhill stair trail to a waterfall
text: Southwest of La Fortuna, near the Fortuna Waterfall, you’ll find a Generation 4 trekker taken by Rainbolt on a downhill trail with many stair segments. It concludes at a [waterfall](https://maps.app.goo.gl/NTT52QT14FChn7Cc9). You can recognise it from his **brown hair** or the **camera crew** following him.
West of La Fortuna, in the Puentes Colgantes Arenal, Mistico Park, there is another trekker on a** tropical trail**, taken by a **black-haired** individual.
clues.summary: Near La Fortuna, a Gen 4 backpack walk goes down a trail with many stairs to a waterfall, with a brown-haired walker and a camera crew. Another trail at a nearby park has a black-haired walker.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 only backpacks and a boat
text: Generation 3 coverage in Costa Rica is **very limited**, consisting of numerous trekkers in and around San José and by the northern west coast. There is also coverage on [Cocos Island](https://goo.gl/maps/RUkuKe4mafK2gbss9), located 500 kilometres southwest of the coast, as well as a boat trekker around [Caño Island](https://goo.gl/maps/CabJDTQ4Cox9ycSQ6) by the southern west coast.
clues.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage is very limited: backpack walks around the capital and the northern west coast, Cocos Island, and a boat near Caño Island.

clues.title: Coverage: beach backpack walks
text: **Beach trekkers** are mostly found on the northern west coast, but can also be found [west of San José](https://maps.app.goo.gl/W1ft4gW7uTFt9zG3A#extra%5Btags%5D=Beach&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng) and on [Cocos Island](https://maps.app.goo.gl/gHZvJaSJNKVMQfFL6#extra%5Btags%5D=Cocos+Forest&extra%5Btags%5D=Beach&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng).
clues.summary: Beach backpack walks are mostly on the northern west coast, but also west of San José and on Cocos Island.

clues.title: Coverage: forest backpack walks in the middle
text: Most rural **forest trekkers** are found in central Costa Rica. [Cocos Island](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cFS241KcJxpjsFP87#extra%5Btags%5D=Cocos+Forest&extra%5Btags%5D=forest&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng) also mainly consists of dense tropical forests.
clues.summary: Most rural forest backpack walks are in central Costa Rica. Cocos Island is mainly dense tropical forest too.

clues.title: Coverage: city streets in a few places
text: **Urban coverage** is mainly found in and around San José and [Cartago](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pJVj27i5NueHCWBC7#extra%5Btags%5D=Cartago&extra%5Btags%5D=aigen&extra%5Btags%5D=urban&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng), but also exists in [Liberia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/FZAENyiYieA99yqi7#extra%5Btags%5D=Costa+Rica&extra%5Btags%5D=pinpointable&extra%5Btags%5D=urban&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng) and [Filadelfia de Guanacaste](https://maps.app.goo.gl/dphFESXufA8G7wwE7#extra%5Btags%5D=Filadelfia+park&extra%5Btags%5D=urban&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng).
clues.summary: City coverage is mainly in and around San José and Cartago, but also Liberia and Filadelfia.

clues.title: Landmark: museum with a castle-like exterior
text: The Children’s Museum in northern San José can be recognised by its grand** castle-like** exterior.
clues.summary: The Children's Museum in northern San José has a grand, castle-like building.

clues.title: Landmark: wealthy homes and a small tower
text: Around the National Museum, you can find several [wealthy-looking homes](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UPPchESTtJpkyJKr6), as well as a small tower built in a style resembling towers on medieval European fortresses.
clues.summary: Around the National Museum you see several wealthy-looking homes and a small tower like those on medieval European fortresses.

clues.title: Landmark: orange footbridge over a highway
text: An **orange pedestrian bridge** can be found going over a major highway at Parque de la Paz in southeastern San José.
While there is [coverage](https://maps.app.goo.gl/5jnT7JS5boCUVQTF8) throughout most of the park, you’re not likely to encounter anything but the bridge in a pinpointable map.

images.caption: An orange footbridge over a highway

clues.summary: An orange pedestrian bridge crosses a major highway at Parque de la Paz in southeastern San José.

clues.title: Park: large park with sports facilities
text: La Sabana Park has several [sports facilities](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8WXHQxLkVboobUpB8), including the National Stadium of Costa Rica, located in the western part of the park.
clues.summary: La Sabana Park has several sports facilities, including the National Stadium, in its western part.

clues.title: Campus: busy, green, medium buildings
text: The University of Costa Rica, in eastern San José, is fairly busy, with a lot of greenery and various medium-sized buildings strewn across the campus.
clues.summary: The University of Costa Rica in eastern San José is busy and green, with many medium-sized buildings across the campus.

clues.title: Stadium: boxy, red, blue and white
text: Palacio de los Deportes is a stadium in Heredia, northwest of San José, which can be recognised by its boxy look combined with the red, blue and white colour scheme.
clues.summary: A stadium in Heredia, northwest of San José, with a boxy shape and a red, blue and white colour scheme.

clues.title: Coverage: backpack on a four-lane road
text: At the Juan Santamaría International Airport you can find the trekker walking in the middle of a major four-lane road. There is also coverage just [outside the airport terminal](https://maps.app.goo.gl/d9V4x5cF5arGJQvK9).
clues.summary: At the main airport the backpack walks in the middle of a big four-lane road. There is also coverage just outside the terminal.

clues.title: Coverage: three dogs follow in pine forest
text: In Centro Recreativo Bosque de la Hoja, just east of San José de la Montaña, you can see the trekker being followed by **three dogs** through a pine forest.
clues.summary: In a recreation centre just east of San José de la Montaña, three dogs follow the backpack through a pine forest.

clues.title: Road: sugarcane and dracaena along the roadside
text: In Recreational Park Los Manantiales, just southwest of Poás, you can find a road lined with sugarcane plantations and [cornstalk dracaena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dracaena_fragrans) plants.
clues.summary: In a recreation park southwest of Poás, a road is lined with sugarcane plantations and cornstalk dracaena plants.

clues.title: Gate: big orange wooden gate at park entrance
text: At the entrance to Laguna de Fraijanes Recreational Park you can find a large **orange wooden gate** separating the road from a parking lot. As the name suggests, the park itself is situated around a [small lagoon](https://maps.app.goo.gl/q9T1iTzTioFFpaY48).
clues.summary: At the entrance to Laguna de Fraijanes park, a large orange wooden gate separates the road from a car park. The park surrounds a small lagoon.

clues.title: Museum: palace-like front with a street railway
text: The Cartago Municipal Museum can be recognised by its **palace-like facade** with a neatly planted garden in front, as well as the railway in the middle of the street in front of the museum.
clues.summary: The Cartago Municipal Museum has a palace-like facade, a neat garden in front, and a railway in the middle of the street.

clues.title: Ruins: remains of a large church
text: The **Ruins of Cartago** is the remains of a large Catholic church near the centre of the city. The POI is one of the first things to show up when you zoom into the city.
clues.summary: The Ruins of Cartago are the remains of a large Catholic church near the city centre, and one of the first things to show up when you zoom into the city.

clues.title: Stadium: surrounded by dark blue walls
text: José Rafael “Fello” Meza Ivankovich Stadium in southern Cartago can be recognised by the **dark blue walls** surrounding it.
clues.summary: A stadium in southern Cartago can be recognised by the dark blue walls around it.

clues.title: Campus: mountain range to the south and east
text: Costa Rica Institute of Technology can usually be recognised by the **mountain range** which can be seen to the south and east.

images.caption: Circle shows a city map; compass in the top middle, beside a road and a bus stop

clues.summary: The Costa Rica Institute of Technology usually shows a mountain range to the south and east.

clues.title: Garden: bad dirt road, mountains, curvy paths
text: By the entrance of Jardín Botanico Lankester, located southeast of Cartago, you can find a poorly maintained dirt road, surrounded by mountains in the distance, as well as a [sign](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ieKVnVBKyytKZxRw5#extra%5Btags%5D=aigen&extra%5Btags%5D=jardin&extra%5Btags%5D=pinpointable&extra%5Btags%5D=urban&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng) with the name of the garden.
Within the garden itself you will find a plethora of different plants, with the [walkways](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZeyMUPjpFPoufVLk9) having many soft curves, and almost never being straight.

images.caption: Circle shows a city map beside a pot-holed road with power poles

clues.summary: At the entrance of the Lankester botanical garden, southeast of Cartago, a poorly kept dirt road runs with mountains in the distance and a name sign. Inside, walkways curve softly and are almost never straight.

clues.title: Resort: red brick paving of Turkish shape
text: The Punta Leona Resort, which can be found by the “Playa Mantas” POI, can be recognised by the **red brick pavement**, with the bricks having the same shape as you’ll commonly find in [Turkey](https://www.google.com/maps/@40.7468922,31.6196471,3a,48.1y,163.7h,64.62t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sxgSFnYGwZ7tHRph3WXoxAA!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: The Punta Leona Resort, near the Playa Mantas POI, has red brick paving with bricks shaped like those common in Turkey.

clues.title: Coverage: white building with round windows
text: The coverage in Liberia can be recognised by a white building with rounded windows having brown wooden window frames. This building can be seen on all coverage in the town.
clues.summary: In Liberia, a white building with rounded windows and brown wooden frames appears in all the coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: park edge with L-shaped red bricks
text: Most of the coverage in Filadelfia de Guanacaste was taken on the edge of a park, with a distinct red brick pavement where the bricks are placed in the shape of an “L”.
clues.summary: Most of the coverage in Filadelfia de Guanacaste is at the edge of a park, with red brick paving laid in L shapes.
